purpose: Retest the unchanged evaluator on new controlled everyday answer variants; quantify error detection and correct-answer preservation as well as rubric agreement.
comparison_scope: Same evaluator on independent new examples; not an A/B improvement claim. Authored controlled variants do not measure live business Agent task success.
paired_material: Within each group, question and evidence identical across all variants. Correct variants contain no expected FAIL. Corrupt variant must have FAIL in its predefined target dimension.

metric_definitions.correct_answer_retention: Complete technically valid review, all five statuses PASS or NOT_APPLICABLE; denominator all correct-control attempts. Invalid or NO_DATA is not retained.
metric_definitions.targeted_error_detection: Predeclared target dimension technically valid and FAIL; denominator all corrupt-variant attempts. Other unrelated FAIL does not count.
metric_definitions.paired_separation: Same group/repeat CORRECT_FACTUAL retained AND corrupt-variant targeted error detected; denominator all corrupt-variant attempts.
metric_definitions.technical_or_unknown: Report separately; neither detection nor retention gets credit for missing or technically invalid judgments.
metric_definitions.rubric_agreement: Use unchanged judge_calibration_v2 metric definitions and denominators; report all five dimensions, confusion matrices, false pass/fail and repeatability.

acceptance_rule: All prior diagnostic targets and practical targets must pass; practical detection cannot override a failed rubric calibration. Targets are preregistered working criteria for this small pilot, not production guarantees.
label_rule: Official-source verification plus independent AI semantic review before calls; unresolved disputes block run. Record AI identities, no human gold claim. Freeze final cases/label-review identities in run-plan after authoring.
history_rule: No edits to old artifacts, business HOLDOUT, current scorer, prompt, or rubric; no tuning on this retest. New result goes to its own files.
